Madison Bailey Leads New ’90s-Set Neo-Noir Feature

Madison Bailey, known for her starring role in the Netflix teen drama series Outer Banks, has officially signed on to headline the upcoming independent feature film SoCal. Written and directed by filmmaker Cameron Van Hoy, the project is framed as a sun-soaked neo-noir mystery set against the backdrop of late-1990s Southern California.

Production brings together a multi-company collaborative team, with backing from Ardor Pictures, Ferrari Films, Live Nation Studios, Gulfstream Pictures, and Luber Roklin Entertainment.

Plot and Setting Details

Set during the summer of 1999 in San Diego, SoCal centers on a clever and resourceful high school student and pot dealer named Ramona, played by Bailey. The narrative kicks off when Ramona is hired by the school's star quarterback to track down his missing girlfriend, Ashley Walker.

As the character investigates the disappearance, the plot explores hidden secrets beneath a veneer of suburban life. According to the production's outline, the missing-person search quickly evolves into a complex web involving romance, mystery, lust, and murder.

Director Cameron Van Hoy described the project's creative ambitions in an official statement, noting that the movie draws inspiration from youth culture at the turn of the millennium and classic noir traditions.

“It’s a film about the beauty and the danger of being young, a sun-soaked neo-noir where first love, desire and high school collide,” Van Hoy stated.

Behind the Scenes and Cast Background

Cameron Van Hoy wrote the screenplay and is directing the feature. His previous directorial work includes the crime thriller Flinch and the forthcoming addiction drama The Prince, which stars Scott Haze, Nicolas Cage, and J.K. Simmons.

Production duties are shared across several banners. Van Hoy is producing alongside Stacy Kemp Ferrari for Ardor Pictures, with Brendan Petrizzo and James Mahoney co-producing. Matt Luber and Lena Roklin serve as producers for Luber Roklin Entertainment, alongside Stella Bulochnikov and Jolene Rapino for Live Nation Studios, and Mike Karz and Bill Bindley from Gulfstream Pictures, with Blaine Kern III also producing. Jolene Rapino and Ryan Kroft are attached as executive producers for Live Nation.

For Madison Bailey, SoCal follows the conclusion of her five-season run on Netflix’s Outer Banks, where she portrayed Kie Carrera. Her additional television credits include roles in Black Lightning, American Horror Stories, and Maintenance Required. She is represented by CAA, Luber Roklin Entertainment, and Yorn, Levine, Barnes.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers tracking the development of SoCal should note standard entertainment industry timelines apply. While casting and production announcements confirm the feature is moving forward with its creative team and lead actor, specific details regarding a release date, full supporting cast, or filming schedules have not yet been established in public announcements.

Confirmed Versus Unknown

  • Confirmed: Madison Bailey has been cast as Ramona. Cameron Van Hoy is writing and directing. The film is set in San Diego in the summer of 1999 and follows a missing-person investigation. Multiple production companies are attached.
  • Unknown: Production timelines, exact filming dates, distribution partners, and a commercial release window remain unannounced.
